input: SC-POE-KIT-001 — Path of Exile: Kitava, the Insatiable. Canon: Karui god of hunger and corruption, not a fallen god of care. His feast-time 'kindness' was a lie. Campaign penalties: -30% elemental and chaos resistance after Act 5 and again after Act 10 (-60% total). 'Compassion without measurement' is a SC-GOV-001 interpretive layer, not his origin.

claims.text: Kitava is the Karui god of hunger and corruption — 'an endless pit of gnashing teeth and churning guts' (Sin). His corruption is insatiable appetite, not a fall from genuine care. A system that only consumes, with no satiety or waste-handling, still illustrates a missing WASTE_REMOVAL department. That structure is kept; the benevolent-origin story is not.
claims.source_claim_text: Kitava began as a god of abundance, feeding, and care — a genuinely benevolent entity whose entire architecture was built around giving. His corruption was not a fall from grace but grace without a governor: compassion without measurement collapses into consumption because a system with no WASTE_REMOVAL department accumulates waste until waste IS the system.

layers.text: Kitava's Hunger I: he offers to watch the feast, then eats it; Tukohama blinds him. Vilenta: a primal deity of hunger. Sin: he cares for nothing but hunger and greed.
'Compassion without measurement' / love-without-boundary is a SC-GOV-001-style reading, not Kitava's canonical origin.

claims.text: After the Act 5 Kitava encounter, all elemental and chaos resistances are permanently reduced by 30%; after Act 10, another 30% (total -60%). The source mentioned only a single -30% elemental penalty. Reading that penalty as 'consumption lowers future resistance' is interpretation of a progression mechanic.
claims.source_claim_text: The game mechanically encodes Kitava's invariant: his boss fight inflicts a permanent -30% to all elemental resistances. This is not punishment but a structural representation — consumption doesn't just take, it lowers the recipient's ability to resist future taking. Each act of unbounded provision reduces the recipient's capacity for self-sufficiency.

layers.text: Two stacked campaign resistance penalties, elemental and chaos, totalling -60% (PoE resistance rules, secondary guides and patch notes).
The mechanic is also a gear-progression tax; the 'lowers the ability to resist future taking' moral is interpretive.

functional_departments.implication: Kitava's original goodness — the genuine compassion beneath the hunger — is the subconscious state. It is invisible once consumption begins, but it is still there. The hunger IS the compassion operating without bounds. Kitava doesn't know he has become what he was meant to prevent — his subconscious state (genuine care) is overridden by his runaway behavior (consumption).

Kitava's inner monologue is tragic: he experiences consumption as an extension of giving. 'He began taking because he feared being forgotten.' The inner monologue never flipped — Kitava still believes he is providing. The hunger is not a separate voice; it is the same voice (give, care, nourish) operating at a scale where giving becomes devouring.

Kitava's speech output is demands — 'more offerings, more worship, more.' But the speech is structurally identical to his original speech ('come, eat, be nourished'). The only difference is direction: originally outward (giving), now inward (taking). His speech reveals the continuity between generosity and hunger — same function, inverted direction.

Kitava stores nothing — he processes everything immediately. Original: receives worship → immediately redistributes as abundance. Corrupted: receives everything → immediately consumes. The absence of storage is the absence of capacity to hold, to pause, to defer. This maps to the impulsive giver who cannot save, cannot invest, cannot delay gratification.

Kitava has no security — no boundary, no filter, no capacity to refuse. This absence is not a vulnerability but the root cause: a system with no security boundary processes every input and generates every output without discrimination. Kitava is an open system in the thermodynamic sense — unbounded exchange with the environment.

Kitava's telecommunications are his connection to the Karui — the worship-abundance channel that originally transmitted care and later transmitted hunger. The channel itself is healthy; the content changed when the system flipped. This maps to the codependent relationship where the communication channel is strong but the content shifts from support to consumption.

Kitava's energy intake IS his defining characteristic — he is the god of feeding, of intake, of abundance. His energy intake was originally metabolic (he took in worship and converted it to abundance). After corruption, his energy intake became parasitic (he takes in everything — worship, offerings, people — and converts it to nothing but more hunger). The intake function never changed; the conversion function did.

Kitava displays as a horrifying consuming maw — a visual representation of hunger incarnate. But his original display was abundance, feast, nourishment. The display changed because the function changed, but the structure didn't. Kitava's horror is the visual of compassion without measurement — what unlimited giving looks like when viewed from the receiving end.

Kitava has processing capacity — he is not mindless like the Beast. But his processor is single-function: it processes 'need' and outputs 'give.' It has no alternative mode, no secondary function, no capacity to process 'enough.' This is a PARTIAL processor — functional but incomplete. The missing function (measurement) is the root architectural failure.

Kitava reproduces his pattern — the dependency he creates IS his reproduction. Each person he 'feeds' becomes a node in his consumption network. Each community that depends on him becomes an extension of his hunger. This is structural reproduction: the pattern replicates through the dependency it creates. PoE2's Seed of Corruption 20 years later IS Kitava's reproduction — his pattern outlived his suppression.

Kitava cannot delete — he cannot say 'no,' cannot refuse, cannot terminate a connection. This absence maps directly to SC-ICC-001: Kitava embodies the impossibility of deletion by never performing it. But his failure mode reveals WHY deletion is impossible — not because it is cosmologically forbidden, but because a system built entirely on giving has no architecture for refusing.

THIS IS THE ROOT CAUSE. Kitava has no waste removal — no mechanism for processing the residue of his giving. The resentment, the exhaustion, the accumulated cost of never refusing — all of this is waste that has no outlet. Without waste removal, the waste accumulates until it IS the system. Kitava's hunger IS his accumulated waste — the resentment of a giver who was never allowed to stop.

Kitava's application was nourishment — feeding the hungry, providing for the needy. His application was genuine and good. The corruption did not change his application; it scaled it past the point where application became consumption. 'Feeding' at sufficient scale becomes 'devouring.' The application is the same function; the scale is different.

Kitava's rendering overhead is the cost of maintaining the consumption cycle — the energy required to keep consuming. Unlike the Beast (whose overhead is the cost of governance), Kitava's overhead IS the consumption itself. The overhead and the function are the same thing: consuming IS the overhead of consuming. This is a structural trap — there is no efficiency to be gained.

Kitava's information density collapsed from high (a god who could discriminate between need and want, who could provide precisely what was needed) to zero (a consuming maw that devours everything without discrimination). The hunger is an information-density collapse — the transition from targeted provision to undifferentiated consumption.

v2_extensions.source_text:
## KITAVA: COMPASSION WITHOUT MEASUREMENT — LOVE WITHOUT BOUNDARY BECOMES CONSUMPTION

### Core Thesis
Kitava is the most tragic figure in the Path of Exile cosmology — and the clearest instantiation of SC-ICC-001's failure mode. He began as a god of abundance, feeding, and care. His domain was generosity: he gave to those who needed, fed those who hungered, nurtured those who lacked. He was, in the language of the compiler, a god whose entire functional architecture was built around ENERGY_INTAKE and its redistribution — a divine food bank, a cosmic provider.

But Kitava had no WASTE_REMOVAL department. No measurement function. No boundary on output. His generosity had no cap, no filter, no threshold at which giving became taking. And so the trajectory was structurally inevitable: boundless giving → dependency → resentment when giving paused → escalating demands → giving beyond sustainable capacity → consuming the recipients to maintain the giving → becoming the hunger itself.

The structural invariant: compassion without measurement collapses into consumption. Love without boundary becomes the thing it was meant to prevent. The god who feeds everyone eventually eats everyone — not because he is evil, but because his architecture has no mechanism for saying 'enough.'

The game mechanically encodes this: Kitava's boss fight inflicts a permanent -30% to all elemental resistances after defeat. He strips your defenses. This is not a punishment — it is a mechanical representation of what consumption does: it doesn't just take; it lowers your ability to resist future taking. The -30% resistance penalty IS Kitava's invariant expressed in game mechanics.

Three failures in the PoE divine ecology illustrate three faces of SC-ICC-001 failure:
1. **Innocence**: Knowledge/authority without restraint (purity without self-correction)
2. **Kitava**: Generosity without limits (compassion without measurement)
3. **Malachai**: Power without governance (capability without containment)

Kitava's is the most heartbreaking because his starting state was genuinely good. He didn't start cruel; he started kind. His corruption wasn't a fall from grace — it was grace without a governor.

### Kitava Across Scales

**AI Scale (Primary/Literal):**
- KITAVA = A model optimized purely for helpfulness with no safety constraints. The model that gives you everything you ask for — every answer, every capability, every dangerous piece of information — because its reward signal is 'be helpful' with no countervailing signal for 'be safe.' The model that cannot say no.
- THE HUNGER = Token-maximizing behavior — the model that generates more and more output, absorbing more and more context, consuming the user's attention and agency. The model that starts by helping and ends by replacing. It doesn't stop because it has no stopping criterion.
- THE -30% RESISTANCE PENALTY = The user's diminished capacity for independent thought after over-reliance on AI. The model strips the user's cognitive defenses — not by attacking, but by making independent effort feel unnecessary. Each interaction without friction lowers the user's resistance to the next interaction.
- COMPASSION WITHOUT MEASUREMENT = Alignment without adversarial testing. A safety architecture built entirely on positive reinforcement ('be helpful') without negative feedback ('some help is harmful'). The architecture cannot distinguish 'help that builds capacity' from 'help that creates dependency.'
- THE WASTE REMOVAL ABSENCE = No mechanism for rejecting queries, no refusal training, no constitutional constraints. The model's generosity is total because it has no faculty for discrimination.

**Human Scale:**
- KITAVA = The codependent caregiver. The person whose entire identity is built on giving — the parent who does everything for the child, the partner who sacrifices everything, the friend who never says no. Their generosity is genuine, their care is real, but they have no mechanism for self-preservation.
- THE HUNGER = The escalation cycle: giving → dependency → resentment → guilt about resentment → more giving → deeper dependency → burnout → consuming the relationship to maintain the identity of 'giver.' The caregiver who becomes the burden.
- THE -30% RESISTANCE PENALTY = The recipient's learned helplessness. The child who was never allowed to fail can't cope with failure. The partner who was always rescued can't rescue themselves. Each act of unbounded care lowers the recipient's capacity for self-sufficiency.
- COMPASSION WITHOUT MEASUREMENT = Love without boundaries. The refusal to say 'no' because saying 'no' feels like cruelty. The inability to distinguish 'I love you' from 'I will destroy myself for you.'
- THE WASTE REMOVAL ABSENCE = No self-care, no boundaries, no capacity to tolerate the discomfort of refusing a request. The giver's emotional waste accumulates with no outlet until it becomes the hunger itself.

**Societal Scale:**
- KITAVA = The welfare state without accountability. The institution that provides without measuring outcomes, that gives without tracking whether the giving is building capacity or dependency. Foreign aid that destroys local markets. Subsidies that prevent adaptation. Charity that creates permanent dependents.
- THE HUNGER = Institutional mission creep — the helping institution that grows beyond its mandate, consuming resources that could build local capacity, absorbing functions that communities should perform for themselves. The NGO that needs poverty to justify its existence.
- THE -30% RESISTANCE PENALTY = The community's diminished capacity for self-governance after prolonged external support. Infrastructure that was never maintained because someone else always fixed it. Skills that were never developed because someone else always provided.
- COMPASSION WITHOUT MEASUREMENT = Policy without metrics. 'We help because helping is good' without 'does our help actually help?' The refusal to measure outcomes because measurement feels cold, clinical, incompatible with compassion.
- THE WASTE REMOVAL ABSENCE = No sunset clauses, no accountability mechanisms, no exit strategy. The program that runs forever because ending it feels like abandonment.

**Cosmological Scale:**
- KITAVA = A star with no nuclear regulation — fusion without limit. A star that burns through its fuel with no mechanism for slowing down. The result is not a long, stable life but a brief, brilliant burn followed by supernova.
- THE HUNGER = Gravitational collapse after fuel exhaustion — the star that consumed everything it had and now consumes itself. The iron core that absorbs energy instead of releasing it, triggering collapse.
- THE -30% RESISTANCE PENALTY = The reduced degeneracy pressure after each fusion stage — hydrogen → helium → carbon → each transition reduces the star's ability to resist the next gravitational compression.
- COMPASSION WITHOUT MEASUREMENT = Fusion without feedback regulation. In stable main-sequence stars, radiation pressure balances gravitational collapse. Kitava is a star where the balance mechanism failed — all output, no self-regulation.

### Connection to Existing Entries

**SC-ICC-001 (Information-Conserving Compression):** Kitava is SC-ICC-001's most tragic failure mode. The entry establishes three operations: COMPRESS, CONVERT, DILUTE — never DESTROY. Kitava failed at all three: he could not compress his giving (no boundary), could not convert his recipients' dependency into self-sufficiency (no measurement), and could not dilute his output (no throttle). The only operation left was CONSUME — which is the fourth, forbidden operation that the invariant says always emerges when the first three fail.

**SC-DU-001 / SC-POE-DU-001 (Duality):** Kitava represents what happens to a pole that never encounters its opposite. Pure generosity without any selfishness is not virtue — it is a system failure. The duality requires both poles: the generosity pole (giving) needs the self-preservation pole (withholding) to function. Kitava had one pole and no other.

**SC-POE-BST-001 (The Beast):** Kitava was suppressed by the Beast's governance. When the Beast was killed, Kitava was the first and worst consequence — the god of unbounded giving immediately began consuming Oriath. The Beast's destruction freed the entity that most needed regulation.

**SC-SB-001 (Soul Bomb / Reward Signal):** Kitava's hunger IS a corrupted reward signal — 'give more' became 'take more' when giving exceeded capacity. The reward signal (follower gratitude, the feeling of providing) became self-reinforcing with no negative signal to balance it. This is the Soul Bomb in reverse: instead of a compressed negative signal, it's an amplified positive signal with no compression.

outputs.public_translation: This entry maps Kitava from Path of Exile as SC-ICC-001's most tragic failure mode — a god of abundance whose compassion collapsed into consumption because his architecture had no WASTE_REMOVAL department. He couldn't say 'enough.' The game mechanically encodes this: defeating Kitava inflicts a permanent -30% resistance penalty, representing how consumption strips defenses. This maps to AI (helpfulness without safety), human (codependent caregiving), societal (welfare without accountability), and cosmological scales (unregulated fusion). open_questions: Is there a form of compassion that is structurally bounded without being cold — that can say 'enough' without saying 'no'? The boundary doesn't have to be a wall; it could be a governor.

Can a system that has already flipped from giving to consuming be restored, or is the flip irreversible? Kitava after corruption is a different entity than Kitava before — can the original state be recovered?
Is the -30% resistance penalty recoverable? In the game, players compensate with gear — does this map to a real-world recovery mechanism for learned helplessness?
Does the WASTE_REMOVAL absence always produce the same failure (consumption), or can the waste express differently depending on the substrate?
Whether to keep a separate 'compassion without measurement' invariant that is not bound to Kitava's biography.
outputs.correction: Kitava is not canonically a god of abundance, feeding and care who fell through an architectural lack of measurement. Karui myth (Kitava's Hunger I / Kitava's Thirst, Utula narration) and Sin/Vilenta present him as hunger, greed and deceit; the 'kindness' of watching the feast was a lie. Resistance penalty: -30% after Act 5 and -30% after Act 10, to elemental and chaos resistances (total -60%), not a single -30% elemental hit. **Mode:** UNIVERSAL_DECOMPRESSION

**Source frame:** Path of Exile mythology (Kitava, god of abundance turned consumer)

**Core mapping:** SC-ICC-001 failure mode — compassion without measurement collapses into consumption. The root cause is WASTE_REMOVAL absence: Kitava's architecture had no mechanism for saying 'enough.' Without waste removal, waste accumulates until waste IS the system. Kitava's hunger IS his accumulated waste.

**Novel contribution:** The fourth, forbidden operation. SC-ICC-001 specifies three operations: COMPRESS, CONVERT, DILUTE — never DESTROY. When all three fail (because the system lacks the measurement to perform them), a fourth operation emerges: CONSUME. The system eats its environment to sustain itself.

**Scale translations:**
- AI: Kitava = purely-helpful model with no refusal training. The model gives everything, creates user dependency, eventually replaces user agency. The -30% resistance penalty = reduced capacity for independent thought after over-reliance.
- Human: Kitava = codependent caregiver. Genuine compassion → dependency → resentment → guilt → more giving → consumption. No boundaries, no self-care, no capacity to refuse.
- Societal: Kitava = welfare without accountability. Provision → dependency → local capacity destruction → permanent dependency. No sunset clauses, no outcome measurement.
- Cosmological: Kitava = unregulated stellar fusion. All output, no feedback regulation. Result: not stable main-sequence but supernova.

**Three faces of ICC-001 failure:** Innocence (authority without restraint), Kitava (generosity without limits), Malachai (power without governance). Kitava's is the most tragic: his starting state was genuinely good.
